name: Dropbox
appType: Scoped-access app (App folder or Full Dropbox)
summary: Works right away in Development status, but a clock starts at 50 linked users: you then have two weeks to win Production approval or new links freeze. Review checks least-privilege permissions, branding and a privacy policy; Dropbox says it answers nearly all requests within a few business days.

composio.note: Composio's managed app lets users connect today. Bring your own for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes or your own rate limits.

steps.title: Create a scoped app in the App Console
steps.detail: Choose **App folder** unless the agent truly needs the whole Dropbox: reviewers reject broader access than the features need.
steps.agent: Recommend App folder vs Full Dropbox from your features

steps.title: Set permissions and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Permissions tab: tick only the scopes you use. Settings: add redirect URIs (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Configure scopes and test the OAuth flow with PKCE

steps.title: Fix branding and publish an app-specific privacy policy
steps.detail: Follow the developer branding guidelines (don't lead your name with "Dropbox") and say what the app will and won't do with user data.
steps.agent: Draft the privacy policy and check names/logos against the guidelines

steps.title: Reach 50 linked users
steps.detail: You can apply any time, but Dropbox won't review until 50 users are linked. From the 50th link you have **two weeks** before new links freeze.

steps.title: Apply for production status
steps.detail: App Console → Apply for production. Explain how the app uses the API, upload an icon, and mention planned features that justify broader permissions.
steps.agent: Write the application text and permission justifications

launchToday: Your own app serves 50 users with no review. Submit the production application early so the 2-week clock never bites.
rejections: Requests Full Dropbox when an App folder would do
Breaks the branding guidelines (e.g. app name starting with Dropbox)
App type on Dropbox's not-allowed list

blockers.fix: You passed 50 users without production approval inside two weeks. Apply (or follow up on the pending request); links resume once approved.

blockers.problem: Need to rename the app after approval
blockers.fix: Production apps can't be renamed by you. Open an API support ticket.

uncertain: "A few business days" is Dropbox's own statement; we haven't measured it.
Team (Business API) apps have separate development limits that the cited guide doesn't cover in detail.
